modules.title: BackButton
modules.description: A round glass "Back" button for mobile that navigates to a fixed path.
modules.body:
A round glass "Back" button that navigates to a fixed path. It is mobile-only:
at widths of 641px and up it renders `display: none`, because desktop has its
own navigation. Usually you don't render it yourself: pass `back` to `Page`.

Use something else for: any other action (`Button`), header actions
(`PageActionsMenu` / `PageActionsBar`, also via `Page`).

## Usage

### Navigation

- **It pushes `to`, it does not go back in history.** Click (or Enter / Space)
  calls `navigate(to, { state: { restoreScroll: true } })`: a new history entry,
  with a state flag asking the destination's scroll manager to restore its
  remembered position instead of jumping to the top.
- Requires a `react-router` (v8, a peer dependency) router above it; it calls
  `useNavigate()` and throws without one.

### Appearance

- Renders a `<div role="button" tabIndex={0} aria-label="Back">` with a
  left-pointing chevron, 46×46px, `radius.circle`, `recipe.glass`.
- It does not position itself. `Page` puts it in its sticky controls row; if
  you render it elsewhere, you place it.
- That is the whole API. No `className`, no label, no `onClick`.

## Do / don't

- Do use `Page back="…"` instead of rendering `BackButton` directly, so it lines
  up with the mobile actions menu.
- Do pass the logical parent route (`/library`, the book page), not a guess at
  the previous URL: it always goes to `to`.
- Don't expect it on desktop; it is hidden at 641px and up.
- Don't wrap it in a `<button>` or `<a>`, or try to restyle it: there is no
  `className`.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
A round glass button that pushes `to` as a new history entry, asking the
destination to restore its scroll position. It does not go back in history,
so pass the logical parent route. Mobile only: it is hidden at 641px and up,
where the desktop navigation takes over. It does not position itself, so you
place it in your own row.

examples.title: In a page
examples.description:
Usually you do not render it yourself: pass `back` to `Page`, which puts the
button in its sticky controls row on mobile, beside the page's actions menu
(`headerActions`).

rows.name: to
rows.description: Path to navigate to. Pushes a new history entry (it does not go back in history), asking the destination to restore its scroll position.

modules.title: Button
modules.description: A clickable action with a visual variant, optional icons, and a loading state.
modules.importLine: import { Button, type ButtonProps, type ButtonRadiusValue, type ButtonTypeValue } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A clickable action with a visual variant, optional icons, and a loading state.
Renders a `<div role="button">` (keyboard: Enter and Space, which it
preventDefaults, so Space does not scroll the page) unless `submit` is
set, in which case it renders a native `<button type="submit">`.

Use something else for: navigating back (`BackButton`), page-level actions in
the header (`PageActionsBar`, `PageActionsMenu`), sticky footer actions
(`PageFooterActions`), picking one of several options (`SegmentedControl`).

## Usage

### Choosing a variant

- `primary`: the one main action of a card, modal, or page (Save, Confirm).
- `default`: secondary actions; bordered.
- `text`: Cancel in a modal footer.
- `link`: inline row actions (Remove, Load more). It has no padding, so `radius`
  doesn't matter for it.
- `dashed`: an "add a row" affordance (as in `FieldList`).
- Add `danger` for destructive actions (Delete, Log out), on `primary` in a
  confirm or on `default` otherwise.

### Corners

The radius follows where the button sits (16px on a page, 8px in a `Card` or
`Dialog`, 4px in a `Popover` or nested Card), so pass no `radius`; see
[corners](../corners.md). Pass it only to override.

### Submitting a form

`submit` renders a native submit button and `onClick` is then ignored: handle
the form's `action` or `onSubmit`. For a button outside its form (a `Card`
footer), pass the form's id as `form`. While the form action is pending the
button shows its spinner by itself.

## Do / don't

- Don't set `radius` to match the surface; it follows depth. Pass it only to
  override.
- Do give repeated row actions a distinguishing `ariaLabel` ("Remove Kindle").
- Don't pass `type="submit"`: it is not a valid variant. Use `submit`.
- Don't pass `onClick` to a submit button and expect it to run.
- Don't pass an element to `prefix`/`suffix` (`prefix={<SearchIcon />}`); pass
  the component.
- Don't wrap Button in a `<button>` or `<a>`: it is already interactive.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
One `primary` action for the main step and a `default` button beside it.
`onClick` takes no arguments: the button passes no event.

examples.title: Variants
examples.description:
`type` picks the look, not the HTML attribute. `primary` is the one main action,
`default` a secondary one, `text` a Cancel in a modal footer, `link` an inline
row action, and `dashed` an "add a row" affordance.

examples.title: Danger and success
examples.description:
Add `danger` to a destructive action: on `primary` when it confirms the
deletion, on `default` otherwise. `success` is the green treatment. The two
cannot both be set; TypeScript rejects it.

examples.title: Icons
examples.description:
`prefix` and `suffix` take an icon component (`prefix={SearchIcon}`), not an
element. An icon-only button needs an `ariaLabel` so it has an accessible name.

examples.title: Loading and disabled
examples.description:
`loading` swaps the icons for a spinner and blocks clicks; `disabled` greys the
button out. Both take the button out of the tab order.

examples.title: Submit button in a card footer
examples.description:
`submit` renders a native submit button; `form` points it at a form elsewhere
in the card. `onClick` is ignored on a submit button, so handle the form's
`action`. Inside a Card the corners step down by themselves: no `radius` prop.

examples.title: Confirm dialog footer
examples.description:
A `text` Cancel beside a `primary danger` action. `loading` shows the spinner
and blocks a second click while the deletion runs; `canDismiss={!deleting}`
keeps the dialog open until it finishes. Inside a Dialog the corners step down
by themselves: no `radius` prop.

rows.description: Native tooltip; passed through.

changelog.text: Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.
The internal `ButtonRadiusContext` is removed; Dialog footer Buttons are unchanged (8px).

`Button` takes a `ref` and `ariaHasPopup`. Its interactive `<div role="button">` now defaults to `tabIndex={0}` so it is reachable by keyboard (`-1` when disabled or loading; an explicit `tabIndex` wins). Its keydown now calls `preventDefault()` on Enter and Space, so Space no longer scrolls the page and Enter opening a menu does not also activate its first item.

Buttons in a `Dialog` footer default to `radius="modal"`; an explicit `radius` still wins. The radius applies to the footer only (a Dialog nested in a footer is unaffected), and `footer={false}`, `''` and `null` render no footer bar.

modules.title: ChipsInput
modules.description: A tag field: the values show as coloured chips in an input box, typing filters a suggestion dropdown, and Enter adds a chip.
modules.importLine: import { ChipsInput, type ChipColor, type ChipsInputProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A tag field: the current values render as coloured chips inside an input box,
typing filters a suggestion dropdown (a `Popover`), and Enter adds a chip. Fully
controlled: you own the `string[]`.

Use something else for: one value from a list (`Select`), one of a few fixed
options (`SegmentedControl`), free text (`TextInput`).

## Usage

### Keyboard

- ArrowDown / ArrowUp move the highlight; Enter or Tab adds the highlighted
  suggestion, else (with `allowCustom`) the trimmed typed text.
- **Tab with text typed adds a chip and keeps focus in the field** (it calls
  `preventDefault`); Tab on an empty field moves focus normally.
- Enter never submits the surrounding form while text is typed, even when
  nothing could be added.
- Backspace on an empty field removes the last chip.
- A value that matches an existing chip case-insensitively is not added.

### Styling

No `className`. The label is linked to the input with a generated id.

## Do / don't

- Do set `layout="horizontal"` and `dense` when it sits among other form fields
  in a `Card`; otherwise the label silently disappears.
- Do pick a `chipColor` that matches how the same values are tagged elsewhere.
- Do use it inside a `Dialog`: the dropdown opens inside the open dialog, so it
  is not hidden behind it (see [popover](popover.md)).
- Don't rely on `name` for form submission.

A controlled tag box in a `Card`. Typing filters the suggestions and Enter
adds the highlighted one, or the typed text; Backspace on an empty field
removes the last chip. `onChange` receives the whole new array, not an event.

examples.description:
Enter or Tab also adds text that matches no suggestion. With
`allowCustom={false}` only a suggestion can be added: unmatched text stays in
the field.

`block` is the bare box and shows no label, even when `label` is set.
`horizontal` and `vertical` add the label on a header row, like the other

`chipColor` picks the colour family for a field's chips. Use the one that
tags the same values elsewhere in the app, so a subject looks like a subject
everywhere.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.description:
`disabled` blocks typing and turns the chips' remove buttons off. A switch
toggles it so both states can be tried.

Among other fields in a `Card`, set `layout="horizontal"` and `dense` so the
label shows and the height matches a `TextInput`. `allowCustom={false}`
restricts it to known users, `chipColor="user"` matches how users are tagged
elsewhere, and `placeholder` and `disabled` follow the loading state. `name`
is set on the text input only: form data gets the half-typed text, so submit
the chips from state.

The suggestion list opens inside an open `Dialog` that contains the field,

changelog.text: `Popover` renders inside an open `<dialog>` that contains its anchor, so `Select` and `ChipsInput` work in modals.

`Popover`:
  - `side` (`bottom`/`top`) and `align` (`start`/`center`/`end`).
  - Flips when the preferred side has no room.
  - Stays inside the viewport horizontally, unless `matchWidth` (then it lines up with the anchor exactly).
  - On the top side it is anchored by its bottom edge, and it re-measures when its content resizes (`ResizeObserver`), so it stays attached as content grows or shrinks.
  - The provisional first render is transparent rather than hidden, so an `autoFocus` child takes focus.
  - Exposes `data-side`.
  - Escape calls `onClose` unless already handled, without closing a surrounding dialog.
  - Defaults keep the same position when there is room below; `Select` and `ChipsInput` now open upward near the bottom of the viewport.

modules.title: DateTimeInput
modules.description: A date with an optional time, edited through the browser's native pickers and stored as an ISO 8601 string.
modules.body:
A date with an optional time, edited through the browser's native date and time
pickers and stored as an ISO 8601 string. The time box stays disabled until
there is a date; clearing the date clears the time.

Use something else for: free text (`TextInput`), a year-only number
(`NumberInput`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

No `className`, no `disabled`, no `min` / `max`.

### Value format

| User has | `onChange` receives |
|---|---|
| no date | `undefined` |
| a date only | `'2023-06-06'` |
| date and time | `'2023-06-06T16:30:00Z'` |

- **The time is UTC, not local.** A stored `2015-08-04T22:30:00-05:00` displays
  as 2015-08-05, 03:30, and the user picks times in UTC too.
- Year and year-month values display as the 1st of the period (`1965` shows
  1965-01-01). Merely displaying doesn't rewrite them; editing does.
- An unreadable value (`'June 2023'`, `'2023-13-45'`) displays as empty.
- Native form data holds the date and the time as **two separate fields**
  (`name`, `nameTime`), not the composed value. Submit `value` from state.

## Do / don't

- Do keep the composed string from `onChange` in state and send that.
- Do tell users times are UTC if that matters for the field.
- Don't read `FormData.get(name)` expecting a timestamp; it is only the date part.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
A date with an optional time. Both come from the browser's native pickers; the time
box stays disabled until there is a date. `onChange` receives the recomposed ISO string,
not an event, and `undefined` once the date is cleared.

examples.description:
`horizontal` and `vertical` paint a shaded row, with the label beside the inputs or
above them. `inline` paints no row, for a spot inside your own layout.

examples.title: Stored values
examples.description:
`value` is an ISO 8601 string as a server stores it, and the inputs re-sync when it
changes. A year or year-month shows as the 1st of the period, a timestamp shows in UTC
(22:30 at -05:00 is 03:30 the next day), and an unreadable string or `''` shows as empty.
Pick a sample, then edit the date to see what `onChange` sends back.

examples.title: In a Card
examples.description:
A form field beside the others in a Card. Keep the composed string from
`onChange` in state and send that: native form data holds the date and the time as
two separate fields (`publishDate`, `publishDateTime`).

rows.description: `'horizontal'` and `'vertical'` paint a shaded row (`bg.cardHeader`, `radius.md`); `'inline'` paints none.

rows.name: onChange
rows.description: Receives the recomposed ISO string (time in UTC), or `undefined` when the date is cleared; not an event.

rows.name: value
rows.description: An ISO 8601 date string as the server stores it: a bare date, a timestamp, or a lower-precision year / year-month. `undefined` and `''` both mean "no date". The inputs re-sync when this changes.

modules.title: FieldList
modules.description: An editable list of rows of text and number inputs, each with a remove button, plus an add button.
modules.importLine: import { FieldList, type ColumnDescriptor, type FieldListProps, type FieldRow } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
An editable list of rows, each with one or more text/number inputs and a
remove button, plus a dashed "add" button underneath. Fully controlled: you own
the rows and apply every change. On phones a row's columns stack.

Use something else for: a list of single words or tags (`ChipsInput`), a fixed
set of fields (`TextInput` / `NumberInput` directly).

## Usage

### Columns

A text column renders a `TextInput`, a number column a `NumberInput` (see
those docs for the controlled-ish behaviour). A number column shows a row value
only if it is a `number`; a numeric string displays as empty.

### Corners

The add button follows surface depth: 16px directly on a Page, 8px in a Card
or Dialog, 4px deeper (8px with no Page, Dialog, Card, CardRow, Alert or Surface above it).

### Behaviour to know

- The add button is 8px outside any surface and follows surface depth inside
  one (a Card body, a Dialog, a Popover).
- Inputs have no labels; use `placeholder` to say what each column is.
- Every remove button is titled "Remove row" (its accessible name); they are not
  distinguished per row.
- No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do generate `_key` once per row (`crypto.randomUUID()`), never from the index.
- Do strip `_key` before sending rows to the server.
- Don't store numeric columns as strings; they won't display.

examples.description:
Rows of inputs with a remove button each and a dashed add button below. You
own the rows: every `onAdd`, `onRemove` and `onChange` is yours to apply, and
each row needs a stable `_key` made once (`crypto.randomUUID()`), never from
the index. Inputs have no labels, so `placeholder` says what each column is.

examples.description:
A `number` column renders a `NumberInput` and reports a `number`, or
`undefined` when the field is emptied; a `text` column reports a string.
`validate` receives the raw text: while it fails, `onChange` is not called
and `onValidChange` reports that field once, when validity flips.

modules.title: Menu
modules.description: A button that opens a list of actions and links, described as data, with keyboard handling built in.
modules.importLine: import { Menu, type MenuActionItem, type MenuIntentProps, type MenuItem, type MenuLinkItem, type MenuProps, type MenuTriggerProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A button that opens a list of actions and links, described as data, with keyboard
handling built in. It follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern. You render the
trigger; Menu gives it the props it needs, draws the
list in a [`Popover`](popover.md) anchored to it, and handles focus and the
keyboard. Pass the items in `items`. There are no child
components and no style file to write.

[`PageActionsBar`](page-actions-bar.md) and [`PageActionsMenu`](page-actions-menu.md)
are built on Menu.

Use something else for: choosing a value ([`Select`](select.md)), page-header
actions ([`PageActionsBar`](page-actions-bar.md) on desktop,
[`PageActionsMenu`](page-actions-menu.md) on mobile).

## Usage

### The trigger

`MenuTriggerProps` is `{ ref, onClick, ariaExpanded, ariaControls, ariaHasPopup: 'menu' }`,
shaped for [`Button`](button.md), so `{...p}` needs no glue. `ref` is a
callback ref (`(node: HTMLElement | null) => void`), so it attaches to any
element without a cast. `ariaControls` is the menu's id while open and
`undefined` while closed. For any other element, pass `ref={p.ref}`, call
`onClick` on click, and map the rest to `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and
`aria-haspopup`; the "Other triggers" example shows it.

### Items

An item is either an action or a link. TypeScript rejects an item with both
`onClick` and `to`, or with neither. Every item takes `label`, `Icon`, `danger`,
`disabled`, `separatorBefore` and `intentProps`; actions add `onClick`, links add
`to`. The tables under Props list each field.

### Keyboard

| Key                                  | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Click, Enter or Space on the trigger | Opens the menu and focuses the first enabled item.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Down / Up                            | Next / previous enabled item, wrapping.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Home / End                           | First / last enabled item.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Enter, Space (or a click)            | Activates the item: the menu closes, focus returns to the trigger, then the action runs or the link navigates.                                                                                                           |
| Escape                               | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Tab / Shift+Tab                      | Closes the menu; focus moves to the tabbable element after / before the trigger, skipping inert and hidden ones. Inside an open `<dialog>` it stays within the dialog; with nothing there, focus returns to the trigger. |
| Pointer-down outside                 | Closes the menu without moving focus.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Behaviour to know

- Escape and outside presses go to the innermost open layer first: a Select
  list opened over the menu closes before it, and a Menu inside a
  [`Dialog`](dialog.md) closes before the Dialog.
- Opening another Menu closes the first (the press on its trigger is outside).
- If the focused item disappears while the menu is open, focus moves to the
  first enabled item. With every item disabled, the menu itself takes focus.
- The menu sits `space.sm` from the trigger and portals out of clipping
  ancestors (into an open `<dialog>` when inside one).

## Do / don't

- Do use Menu for any list of actions or links behind a button.
- Do pass icon components (`Icon: BookIcon`), not elements.
- Don't hand-build `role="menu"`, or wire a Popover and buttons yourself.
- Don't wrap the trigger in another `<button>`; spread the props onto it.

changelog.text: Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

**Visible changes:**
  - Buttons in a Card default to 8px (they were 16px unless `radius="card"` was set), and Buttons in a Dialog body are 8px.
  - Selects directly on a Page get the page look (16px and the card shadow); in a Card or Dialog they stay 8px. This includes Selects in your own boxes on a Page (a `useModalDialog` modal, a `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` box), because depth cannot see hand-drawn boxes: wrap their contents in `Surface`, or pass `surface="card"`.
  - Without a Page, a bare `Card` counts as depth 0: its Buttons go from 16px to 8px, a Card nested in it steps down, and a `CardRow` in it is 8px.
  - A Card nested in a Card or Dialog steps down (8px, then 4px), and so do its Buttons and Selects; `size="small"` keeps its extra 1px.
  - `CardRow` is 16px on a Page and 8px inside a Card (it was always 16px).
  - Buttons and Selects inside a Popover or Menu are 4px.

`theme.space` values are typed as `SpaceValue` (`${number}rem`), so `gap={theme.space.sm}` on `Popover` and `Menu` needs no `as PopoverGap` cast. `Theme['space']` is now typed `${number}rem`, so hand-built Theme objects or mocks with `px` values stop type-checking.

New `Menu` (control): a button that opens a list of actions and links, described as an `items` array (`onClick` for actions, `to` for links; `Icon`, `danger`, `disabled`, `separatorBefore`, `intentProps`). Arrow keys, Home and End move between items, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. `surface` is `solid` or `glass`.

`Menu` trigger props: `ref` is a callback ref, so it attaches to a `<button>`, an `<a>` or a `Button` without a cast; `ariaControls` is set only while the menu is open. Tab from an open menu skips inert, hidden and `tabindex="-1"` elements and stays inside an open `<dialog>`. A disabled link item has no `href`.

`PageActionsMenu` and `PageActionsBar` are rebuilt on `Menu`: arrow keys, Home and End move between actions, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. `PageActionItem` is now `MenuActionItem & { primary?, align? }`: it gains an optional `Icon` (shown in the menus, ignored by the bar's primary Buttons), and `to` is not allowed.

modules.title: NumberInput
modules.description: A single-line field that reports a number, with a label and validation.
modules.body:
A single-line field for a number, with an optional label and validation. It
parses with `parseFloat` and reports `number | undefined`. Same label/layout
system as `TextInput`.

Use something else for: one of a few fixed numbers (`SegmentedControl` or
`Select`), free text (`TextInput`).

## Usage

### Behaviour to know

- It is a plain `<input>` (no `type="number"`, no `inputMode`), so phones show
  the full text keyboard and there are no spinner arrows.
- The default check accepts text that both `Number()` and `parseFloat` read as a
  number: `1.5`, `-3`, `1e3` (reported as `1000`). `onChange` sends `parseFloat`
  of the text, so `0x10` passes but is reported as `0`.
- Invalid text stays visible with a red label and border; your state keeps the
  last valid number.

### What it has no prop for

No `className`, no `disabled`, no `min` / `max` / `step`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `label={undefined}` explicitly when there is no visible label.
- Do report `onValidChange` into the form and disable submit while any field is invalid.
- Don't expect integer-only input unless your `validate` enforces it.

Without `validate` the field accepts empty text or text that both `Number()` and
`parseFloat` read as a number: try `1.5`, `-3` or `1e3` (reported as 1000).
`onChange` sends `parseFloat` of the text, so `0x10` passes but is reported
as 0. Other text turns the
label and border red, `onValidChange` fires once, and `onChange` is not called,
so the saved number stays at the last valid one. Type `abc` to see it.

The `horizontal` layout is made for a `Card` body. Index uses the built-in check.
Width replaces it with a rule that still checks the text is numeric, and both

either is invalid.

modules.description: A single-value dropdown with type-to-search, an optional "Add: …" entry for new values, a clear button, and a loading state.
modules.importLine: import { Select, type SelectOption, type SelectProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A single-value dropdown with type-to-search (on by default), an optional "Add:
…" entry for new values, a clear button, and a loading state. The dropdown is a
`Popover`, so it escapes clipping cards.

Use something else for: 2–5 options that fit in one row (`SegmentedControl`),
several values (`ChipsInput`), on/off (`Switch`).

## Usage

### Choosing a surface

Follow [corners](../corners.md):

- Usually omit it: the default follows where the select sits. Directly on a
  `Page` it is `'page'`; in a card or dialog (and outside any surface) it is
  `'card'`; two or more surfaces deep it is `'inset'`.
- `'card'`: `radius.md`, no shadow.
- `'page'`: `radius.lg` + `shadow.cardStack`, like a card.
- `'inset'`: `radius.sm`, no shadow, for a select nested inside an inset box.
- Pass `surface` only to override the depth.

### Forms

There is no hidden input carrying `value`: native `FormData` will not contain
the selection (only the search text while open). Keep `value` in state and
submit that. The `<label>` targets the search box, so it is not the closed
trigger's accessible name; the trigger announces the selected label or
placeholder.

### Keyboard

Closed: Enter, Space or ArrowDown open it. Open: ArrowUp/ArrowDown move (and
wrap), Enter selects, Escape or Tab close. The highlight starts on the first
option, not the current value.

### Inside a dialog

It works inside a `Dialog` or a modal `<dialog>`: the list opens inside the
open dialog (see [popover](popover.md)).

### Styling

No `className`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `clearable={false}` when an empty value is invalid.
- Don't pass `surface="page"` inside a card; let the depth decide.

modules.title: SegmentedControl
modules.description: A row of equal-width radio segments in a track, with a lens that slides to the checked one.
modules.importLine: import { SegmentedControl, type SegmentedControlProps, type SegmentedOption } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A row of equal-width radio segments in a track, with a lens that slides to the
checked one. Options can be text, or an icon over a small caption. Optionally
clearable, and read-only when `onChange` is omitted. Generic over the value
type: `V extends string`.

Use something else for: many options or long labels (`Select`), on/off
(`Switch`), actions (`Button`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

No `className`, no `name` (not a form field). Type options with the exported
`SegmentedOption<V>` (and props with `SegmentedControlProps<V>`).

### Keyboard

On the group: ArrowRight/ArrowUp and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown step one option and do
not wrap; Home/End jump to the ends; digits 1–9 pick that option; Backspace and
Delete clear when `clearable`. Modified keys (Ctrl/Cmd/Alt) are left alone.

### Choosing a surface

The track and lens are always `radius.md` (see [corners](../corners.md)), so the
control belongs inside a card or modal.

- Directly in a `Card` body: omit `surface` (`'card'`).
- Inside a shaded `bg.cardHeader` row you built (label left, control right):
  `surface="row"`, so the row itself is the track and the lens is flush with it.

## Do / don't

- Do keep it to a handful of short options; segments are equal columns.
- Do pass `clearable` whenever `null` is a valid answer, or the user can never
  get back to it.
- Don't pass `onChange={() => {}}` to show a value; omit `onChange` for read-only.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description:
A few short text options. Declare them `as const` so `value` and `onChange`
are typed to the option values. The `label` names the group for assistive tech
and is not drawn, so put a visible label beside the control yourself.

examples.title: Icons
examples.description:
An option with an `Icon` draws it above its label, which becomes a small
caption. `showLabels={false}` drops the captions and leaves icons only; the
`label` stays each segment's accessible name. `Icon` takes a component
(`ThumbDownIcon`), not an element.

examples.title: Clearable
examples.description:
With `clearable`, clicking the checked segment, Backspace or Delete calls
`onChange(null)`. Once the value is `null` nothing is checked and no lens is
drawn. Without `clearable`, `onChange` never receives `null`.

examples.title: Read-only
examples.description:
Omit `onChange` to show a value without letting it change: the segments are
marked `aria-disabled` and ignore clicks and keys. A `null` value checks
nothing and draws no lens.

examples.title: Surfaces
examples.description:
In a Card body the control paints its own track. In the shaded Card header the
header is the track, so `surface="row"` paints nothing and only the lens
shows. The corner is the same in both: the control belongs inside a card or
modal.

rows.name: clearable
rows.description: Clicking (or Space/Enter on) the checked segment, Backspace and Delete clear the value. Without it, clicking the checked segment does nothing and there is no way to clear.

rows.name: label
rows.description: The group's accessible name (`aria-label`), e.g. the setting it edits. Not rendered visibly: put a visible label beside it yourself.

rows.name: onChange
rows.description: Receives `null` (a clear) only when `clearable` is set. Absent means read-only: the control shows the value, and segments get `aria-disabled` and ignore clicks and keys.

rows.name: options
rows.description: The segments, in order. Declare them `as const` or type them as `SegmentedOption<V>`.

rows.name: showLabels
rows.description: Render each option's label. Only an option with an `Icon` can go without one; a text-only option always shows its label.

rows.name: surface
rows.description: What the control sits on. `card` paints its own `bg.track` rail. `row` paints nothing: the shaded input row it sits in is the track and only the lens shows, the way the white field shows in a `TextInput` row.

rows.name: value
rows.description: The checked option; `null` (or a value no option has) checks nothing and draws no lens.

rows.name: Icon
rows.description: Icon component (`Icon: SearchIcon`), not an element. Drawn above the label, which then becomes a small caption under it.

rows.name: label
rows.description: The segment's accessible name, and its visible text unless `showLabels` is off.

rows.name: value
rows.description: The value passed to `onChange` when this segment is picked.

modules.body:
An on/off toggle (`role="switch"`) with an optional label and description, a
full-row `horizontal` layout for forms, and a `loading` state for saves in
flight. Controlled: you own `checked`.

Use something else for: one of several options (`SegmentedControl`, `Select`),
an action that happens on click (`Button`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

No `className`. Keyboard: Enter and Space toggle. Clicks and those keys stop
propagation, so a switch inside a clickable card row won't trigger the row.

### Choosing a radius

See [corners](../corners.md).

- In a shaded row (`layout="horizontal"`, or inside any field row): omit it
  (`inset`, a 4px track concentric with the row's 8px corner).
- In a `Card` header (`headerAction`), or anywhere with no nearby corner to
  echo: `radius="pill"`.

## Do / don't

- Do pass `loading` while the save runs instead of `disabled`; `disabled` means
  "you may not change this".
- Do give a label-less switch an `ariaLabel`; `name` is a machine key.
- Don't expect a switch to submit with a `<form>`; send `checked` from state.
- Don't put an interactive element in `description` of a `horizontal` switch:
  clicking it toggles the switch.

modules.title: TextInput
modules.description: A single-line text or password field with a label, validation, and a character counter near `maxLength`.
modules.importLine: import { TextInput, type TextInputAction, type TextInputProps } from '@korzun/design/control'
modules.body:
A single-line text (or password) field with an optional label, optional
validation, and a character counter that appears near `maxLength`. The default
`horizontal` layout puts the label and field on one shaded row, which is how
form fields look inside a `Card`.

Use something else for: multi-line text (`TextArea`), numbers (`NumberInput`),
picking from a list (`Select`), a list of tags (`ChipsInput`), dates
(`DateTimeInput`).

## Usage

### Controlled-ish

The field keeps its own text. It re-syncs from `value` only when the `value`
prop changes. While `validate` fails, the field shows the invalid text but
`onChange` is not called, so your state keeps the last valid value. Track
`onValidChange` to block submit.

### What it has no prop for

No `className`, no `disabled`, no `id`.

## Do / don't

- Do keep the default `horizontal` layout for fields in a `Card` body; use
  `vertical` when the label is long or the field is wide.
- Do coalesce `undefined` (`v ?? ''`) if your state is a plain string.
- Don't pass an `action`; render a separate `Button` beside the field instead.
- Don't rely on clicking the label to focus the field; it isn't associated.

modules.title: Alert
modules.description: A tinted box for a status message in the page flow, with an optional title, icon and action.
modules.importLine: import { Alert, type AlertProps, type AlertTone } from '@korzun/design/component'
modules.body:
A tinted, bordered box for a status message that sits in the page flow: a tone,
an optional title, body text, an optional icon and an optional action. The
tone's `theme.color.chip[tone]` colours the background, border, title and icon;
the body text uses the normal text colour so a sentence stays readable.

Use something else for: inline field or form failure text (`ErrorMessage`), or a
single status word in a row (`Tag`). An Alert is for a message with weight that
may carry an action.

## Usage

### Choosing a tone

- `warning`: needs attention (overdue, about to expire).
- `danger`: something failed.
- `success`: something finished.
- `info`: neutral news.

`warning` and `danger` render `role="alert"` and are announced the moment they
mount; `success` and `info` render `role="status"` and are announced politely.

### Behaviour

- Corners follow surface depth (see [corners](../corners.md)): 16px on a Page,
  8px in a Card. With no provider the Alert counts as depth 0.
- Its contents, including `action`, sit one level deeper, so a Button in the
  action is already one step smaller than the Alert. Do not pass `radius`.
- There is no default icon per tone; pass `Icon` when you want one.
- Spacing and font sizes come from theme tokens; there is no `style` prop.

## Do / don't

- Do pick the tone by meaning, not by colour.
- Do put the one recovery action in `action`.
- Don't use it for field errors; use `ErrorMessage`.
- Don't mount a `danger` or `warning` Alert for static, always-visible copy:
  it is announced as an alert when it appears.

changelog.text: Surface depth: corners are concentric site-wide with no radius props. `Page` provides depth 0, `Dialog` 1, and `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where they sit; `Popover` (so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2. Depth 0 is `radius.lg`, 1 is `md`, 2 and deeper is `sm`. `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` follow it; an explicit `Button radius` or `Select surface` still wins. With no `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it, a component keeps its 0.4.0 look; a bare `Card` (no `Page`) still counts as depth 0 and gives its contents depth 1, so its Buttons and nested Cards change as below.

New `Alert` (component): a tinted box with a `tone` (`warning`, `danger`, `success`, `info`), optional `title`, `Icon` and `action`, and body text. `danger` and `warning` get `role="alert"`, `success` and `info` get `role="status"`.

modules.title: MetaLine
modules.description: A row's secondary line: a few short data separated by middots that wrap between data, never inside one.
modules.body:
A row's secondary line: a few short data ("Frank Herbert", "Book 3", "42%")
separated by middots. When too narrow, it wraps *between* data, never inside
one, and never leaves a separator dangling at a line end or leading the next
line. The separators are CSS (`::before`), not text, so screen readers read
only the data.

Use something else for: labelled key/value pairs (`MetadataList`), a row's
primary title (`Text` or `Heading`).

## Usage

### Behaviour

- Only `null`/`undefined`/`false` are skipped. `''` and `0` are kept and draw a
  separator with nothing (or `0`) after it; filter them yourself.
- A single datum wider than the line ellipsizes instead of wrapping.
- Items are keyed by index.

### Typography

MetaLine sets no font size or colour of its own except the separator colour
(`text.muted`); wrap it in `Text` to set the rest.

## Do / don't

- Do pass conditional data as `cond && value`; `false` is skipped.
- Do set typography by wrapping the line in `Text` (`size`, `tone`); the items inherit it.
- Don't join data into one string with your own " · ": wrapping then breaks
  inside a datum and the dots are read aloud.
- Don't pass empty strings; they leave a stray separator.

modules.title: Stack
modules.description: A vertical column with a themed gap between children.
modules.body:
A vertical flex column with a themed gap between children. Use it to space
things on a screen instead of writing a style file: a form's fields, the
sections of a page, the rows of a list.

Use something else for: a horizontal row (`Inline`), a bordered surface
(`Card`), a divider line between items (`CardDivider`), text styling (`Text`,
`Heading`).

## Usage

### Choosing a gap

Pick `gap` from the theme's `space` scale so spacing is the same everywhere:
`xs` for tight groups, `md` for most content, `xxl` between sections.
`gap="none"` emits `gap: 0`, for children that supply their own spacing.

### Behaviour

- `align` is the horizontal (cross-axis) alignment. `stretch` makes children
  full width; `start` keeps buttons and tags at their own width.
- `as="ul"` and `as="ol"` also reset the list's margin, padding and bullets.
  Children should be `li` (`<Stack as="li">` works).
- Every other HTML attribute (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event handlers) passes
  through. There is no `style` prop: spacing comes from tokens only.
- Override with `className` at `'&&'` specificity, never `!important`.
- `as="form"` is not offered. Put a `<form>` around the Stack instead.

## Do / don't

- Do nest a Stack in a Stack for sections with different gaps.
- Do use `align="start"` when children (buttons, tags) should not stretch.
- Don't add margins to children to space them; use `gap`.
- Don't reach for `className` to set a gap; use the prop.
- Don't use a Stack for a row; use `Inline`.

guides.title: Corners
guides.description: Corner radius by nesting depth, one radius step per level.
guides.body:
Corner radius tracks **depth**, not size. Surfaces on the page background have
the roundest corners. Each surface nested inside another gets a squarer,
concentric corner, so the inner curve follows the outer one.

## Tokens

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `theme.radius.lg` | 16px | Surfaces on the page background |
| `theme.radius.md` | 8px | One level in: inside a card or modal; also floating layers |
| `theme.radius.sm` | 4px | Two levels in: inside an input, inset box, row, or menu |
| `theme.radius.pill` | 999px | Capsules: nav bar, a Switch with no nearby corner |
| `theme.radius.circle` | 50% | Round glass buttons |

## The rule

Find where the element sits, then read its radius from this table:

| Where the element sits | Radius | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| On the page background | `lg` | `Card`, modal dialog (`recipe.modal.dialog`), `Button`, `Select` and `CardRow` directly on a `Page` (automatic) |
| Inside a card or modal | `md` | inputs (`recipe.input`), Buttons and Selects in a Card or Dialog (automatic), `Tag`, shaded rows (`recipe.row`), inset boxes |
| Inside one of those | `sm` | a chip inside an input, Buttons and Selects in a nested Card, inset box (`Surface`) or Popover (automatic), a menu item, a Switch track in a shaded row |
| Flush with its parent (zero inset, edges touch) | the parent's radius | an unlabelled Select's trigger, an input filling its row |
| Inset 4px or less from its parent | `calc(parent − inset)` | a Switch thumb 2px inside a 4px track is 2px |
| A small control with no nearby corner | `pill` / `circle` | a Switch in a full-width card header |
| A floating layer (popover, menu, dropdown, toast) | `md`, plus `shadow.hoverLift` or `recipe.glass` | its items are `sm` |

**Step down one token per level** (`lg` → `md` → `sm`). Do not subtract the
padding: a Card has 13px of inset, but the inputs inside it are `md` (8px), not
16 − 13 = 3px. Exact subtraction applies only to tight insets of 4px or less.

## It's automatic

Components read their corners from the **surface depth** they sit at, so you
pass no radius prop:

| Depth | Radius | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `lg` (16px) | On the page background, inside a `Page` |
| 1 | `md` (8px) | Inside a `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Dialog` on the page |
| 2+ | `sm` (4px) | One more level in; deeper levels stay `sm` |
| none | each component's old default | No `Page`, `Dialog`, `Card`, `CardRow`, `Alert` or `Surface` above it (tests, bare stories) |

Who provides depth:

- `Page` provides 0, to its header, content and footer actions.
- `Dialog` provides 1 to its header, body and footer.
- `Card`, `CardRow` and `Alert` each provide one level deeper than where
  they sit, so a Card in a Card steps down.
- `Popover` (and so `Menu` and the `Select` list) provides a fixed 2: a
  floating layer is `md` and its items `sm`, whatever opened it.

What follows depth with no prop: `Button`, `Select`, `Card`, `CardRow`,
`Alert`. For a hand-made box that holds Buttons or Selects, wrap its contents
in `<Surface>` and read its own radius with `useSurfaceRadius()`; see
[surface](component/surface.md).

Hand-drawn boxes (your own `recipe.card.shell` or `recipe.row` styles, a `useModalDialog` modal) are invisible to depth: wrap their contents in `Surface`.

An explicit prop (`Button radius`, `Select surface`) is an **override** and
always wins over depth. It pins that radius even where depth would step down,
which breaks concentricity, so set it only when the surface really is different
(`radius="background"` on a Button that must stay round inside a Card).

`Switch` still takes `radius` (`inset` or `pill`) by hand, and `type="link"`
buttons have no padding or background, so radius doesn't apply.

## In your own styles

```ts
const useStyles = createUseStyles((theme: Theme) => ({
  panel: { ...theme.recipe.card.shell },  // already lg
  inset: {
    backgroundColor: theme.color.bg.cardHeader,
    borderRadius: theme.radius.md,        // one level in
    padding: theme.space.md,
  },
  chip: { borderRadius: theme.radius.sm }, // two levels in
  knob: { borderRadius: `calc(${theme.radius.sm} - 2px)` }, // 2px inset
}));
```

- Never write a literal `borderRadius` (`'12px'`, `'50%'`). The only
  non-token form allowed is `calc(theme.radius.X ± Npx)` for tight insets.
- A 1px inset works the other way too: `Card size="small"` is
  `calc(radius.md + 1px)` so its flush `md` children stay concentric.
